Might seem a little counter-intuitive, but for me one thing that helps put whatever trial lies before me into perspective is visualizing the 'worst case scenario'. e.g. Oh no! My scumbag landlord hired an attorney to represent her in the small claims case I filed. Well, if I lose, I'm looking at what, $4,000 down the drain? Is it going to ruin me forever? No. Is it gonna suck? Yeah, but I can recover and who cares, be tough.

A lot of good points, but two that I'd like to add. I suffer from depression and these are two of the been biggest ones that help me mange to stay positive.

  • exercise - I can't over stress the importance of this. Dragging your ass to exercise can be gruelling when you're caught up in a negative cycle, but the endorphins it dumps into your system and the 'I did something positive today' effect are worth their weight in gold. Physical and emotional states are more strongly linked than we normally credit.

  • fake it - this seems shallow and pointless, but in my experience it is actually vital. I remember seeing research back in university studying facial expression as a cause, not effect of emotional state. I dismissed it as junk at the time because it didn't fit my model of self. I've found however, that faking positive emotional states in my daily interactions, reinforces positivity while honesty reinforces my current mental state which is not always so. When people ask how I'm doing (in a casual sense) I always smile and respond, "excellent" - no matter my reality. Yes, it's fake, but it becomes an affirmation that continuously shifts my perspective in that direction. Proviso - there's a line between healthy affirmation and denial here. You still have to recognize if you're truly in crisis and ask for help if that the case.
